newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Gazprom ally said heading UES stake buy.
newsitem.headline: Gazprom ally said heading UES stake buy.

text.p: A consortium headed by Natsionalny Rezervny Bank, closely linked to Russian gas monopoly Gazprom, bought most of the 8.5 percent of Russian power company Unified Energy System (UES) auctioned recently, a purchasing agent spokesman said on Thursday.
Inkom-Finance Group AG of Switzerland, the finance company of Russia's Inkombank, acted as purchasing agent for the consortium, said Ilya Yakushev, an Inkombank spokesman.
"We bought practically the entire stake," he said, adding that the consortium, through Inkom-Finance, had purchased over 99 percent of shares sold.
A Natsionalny Rezervny Bank spokesman was unavailable for immediate comment. Gazprom owns a major stake in the bank.
Russia sold 8.49 percent of national power company RAO Yedinaya Energeticheskaya Sistema Rossii (UES) for an average 512.82 roubles per share, the Federal Securities Corporation said on Wednesday.

Yakushev said Inkombank was also part of the consortium of buyers, which he said included Russia's biggest oil company LUKoil, two state-owned banks -- Sberbank, and Vneshekonombank -- and a number of other companies.
A UES official said there were no official data yet on the purchaser.
UES, with overall debts of about 50 trillion roubles, owes a substantial sum to Gazprom, a UES spokesman said, but did not name a specific figure.

Shares in UES slipped to $0.1307 at 1025 GMT on Thursday from Wednesday's close of $0.1325. Shares were trading below nine cents each, the approximate auction price, when the auction was announced in November.
